Dirección Nacional de Vialidad (DNV).desc: Argentina's national roads agency. It is a decentralised body under the transport secretariat of the Ministry of Economy, and it plans, builds and maintains the national road network of more than 40,000 kilometres, using its own crews, contractors or concession companies, and supervises the concession holders. A decree of 7 July 2025 began a reorganisation of decentralised agencies including Vialidad, with its existing authorities carrying on their functions in the meantime.

sources.title: Preguntas frecuentes - Vialidad
Resolución 1136/2025, Dirección Nacional de Vialidad
sources.publisher: Boletín Oficial de la República Argentina

Tamiz Shahar JSC.desc: An Azerbaijani joint-stock company that handles the dumping and treatment of household waste in Baku, and since 2021 and 2022 decrees also the collection and disposal of waste in territories retaken by Azerbaijan. It was set up by a presidential decree of 6 August 2008 and registered on 12 March 2009; a presidential order of 22 September 2021 placed it under the management of Azerbaijan Investment Holding. Collecting and carrying Baku's waste stays with the Baku City Executive Power.

sources.title: About us

Ghana Highway Authority.desc: Ghana's state road agency. It was created in December 1974 by decree NRCD 298, which the Ghana Highway Authority Act 1997 (Act 540) replaced while keeping the body in being, and its work is limited to the trunk road network, which its own profile puts at about 15,000 kilometres. It administers, develops and maintains those roads and their bridges, culverts and ferries.

sources.title: Institution Profile
Ghana Highway Authority entity profile
sources.publisher: State Interests and Governance Authority, Ghana

Thimphu Thromde.desc: The city government of Thimphu, Bhutan's capital, covering about 26 square kilometres from Dechencholing in the north to Babesa in the south. A Thromde is an urban local government under Bhutan's Local Government Act 2009 and the Thromde Rules 2011, with duties that include planning, land management, water supply, sewerage, solid waste and local revenue.

sources.title: About Us
Thromde Rules of the Kingdom of Bhutan 2011
sources.publisher: Ministry of Works and Human Settlements, Bhutan

Kribi Power Development Company (KPDC).desc: A Cameroonian electricity company that owns and runs the 216 MW gas-fired power station at Kribi and sells all its output to the national utility under a 20-year contract. It is 56 per cent owned by the power developer Globeleq, which bought the stake previously held by AES, and 44 per cent by the government of Cameroon. Its generating licence covers up to 330 MW.

sources.title: Kribi Power Development Corporation
sources.publisher: Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, World Bank Group

Belize Social Investment Fund.desc: A Belizean public body set up by the government in 1996 under the Social Investment Fund Act (Chapter 43, in force 1 May 1996) as an autonomous corporate institution. It approves and pays for small projects in basic services and infrastructure, health and education facilities, run with community groups, non-governmental organisations and local councils, and is governed by a board whose members a minister appoints. Its funding has come from the government of Belize, the Caribbean Development Bank and the World Bank.

sources.title: Social Investment Fund Act, Chapter 43
History of SIF

Companhia do Metropolitano de São Paulo.desc: The company that builds and runs the São Paulo underground railway, incorporated on 24 April 1968 and controlled by the state government of São Paulo. In 2023 it ran four lines with 63 stations and carried about 851 million passengers.

sources.title: Relatório Integrado 2023
sources.publisher: Companhia do Metropolitano de São Paulo

Consórcio Via Amarela.desc: A temporary grouping of five Brazilian construction companies formed to build Line 4 of the São Paulo underground: OAS, CBPO of the Odebrecht group, Queiroz Galvão, Camargo Corrêa and Andrade Gutierrez.

sources.title: Metrô: Linha 4 tem 46 problemas, dizem fiscais

Companhia de Habitação da Baixada Santis.desc: A public housing company serving the Baixada Santista coastal area of São Paulo state, Brazil. Its work includes building and managing low-cost housing estates, regularising the land and titles under them, collecting and renegotiating housing loan payments, and running housing assistance for families moved out of landslide-risk areas in Santos, with money from municipal, state and federal housing funds.

sources.title: Resumo das Atividades Desenvolvidas no Exercício de 2025 - COHAB-ST
sources.publisher: Central de Balanços, Serpro (Government of Brazil)

China National Electronic Equipment Corp.desc: A Chinese contractor based in Beijing that acts as general contractor on power plant projects and supplies the mechanical and electrical equipment for them. Its general contract with the Botswana Power Corporation for the Morupule B coal-fired plant was reported at about 970 million US dollars.

sources.title: Chinese Company to Build Coal-Fired Plant in Botswana

NEPEC 11.note: Searched for the name on its own and together with Morupule and Botswana. No company page, register entry or news article naming an entity called NEPEC 11 could be opened, so nothing can be said about what it is.

Société Nationale des Hydrocarbures (SNH.desc: Cameroon's state oil and gas company, created on 12 March 1980 to manage the state's interests in the sector, with the state as its sole shareholder. It negotiates and monitors petroleum contracts, develops fields alone or with partners, sells the state's share of production and pays the proceeds to the treasury. In 2020 national crude output was 26.6 million barrels and SNH's oil and gas sales for the state came to 785 million US dollars.

sources.title: Rapport annuel 2020

Wartsila.desc: An engineering group that makes engines, power plants and propulsion and related services for ships and for electricity generation. It is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki, and reports net sales of 6,219 million euros in 2025 and about 17,900 staff in 78 countries.

sources.title: About Wärtsilä

Siemens France.desc: The French arm of the German technology group Siemens AG, working in industry, infrastructure, transport and medical technology. Siemens France Holding, named as the Siemens AG subsidiary there, reported revenue of 1.9 billion euros from continuing operations for the year to 30 September 2021 and about 6,000 staff across four industrial sites and 23 engineering sites.

sources.title: Siemens France press release (company boilerplate)

KEC India.desc: KEC International Limited, an engineering, procurement and construction company based in Mumbai and the flagship firm of India's RPG Group. It builds power transmission and distribution lines, railways, civil works, oil and gas pipelines and renewable plants, and makes transmission towers, poles and cables. It is listed on the BSE and the National Stock Exchange of India, and reported turnover of 191,778 million rupees and 6,543 employees in the year to 31 March 2025.

sources.title: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, FY 2024-25
sources.publisher: KEC International Limited (filed with National Stock Exchange of India)

Delvina Municipality.desc: A municipality in southern Albania, in Vlore county, covering 182.9 square kilometres. It is made up of two administrative units, the town of Delvine and the former commune of Vergo, which were brought together under the Delvine centre. Its total assets stood at about 1.31 billion lek at the end of 2024.

sources.title: Raport i auditimit financiar - Bashkia Delvine
sources.publisher: Kontrolli i Larte i Shtetit (Albanian Supreme State Audit)

Municipality of Shkodra.desc: The city government of Shkoder in northern Albania, run by an elected mayor and a municipal council. Its services cover local planning and building control, environment, local public services, social housing and aid, schools, culture and sport, public transport and a municipal police force, and it sets and collects local taxes and fees.

sources.title: Bashkia Shkoder official website

Ministry of Education and Science.desc: Albania's national education ministry. It drafts education law and bylaws, runs the national education strategy, checks school quality and the use of public funds, sets teacher development policy for pre-university schools, and for universities sets policy and funding, approves new degree programmes and keeps the state register of scientific degrees. The ministry has carried several titles; Albania's education ministry is now styled Ministry of Education, and in recent years also Ministry of Education and Sports.

sources.title: Albania: Administration and governance at central and/or regional level
Ministry of Education official website

Expropriation Commission, Ministry of Pu.note: Searched Albanian legislation (including the expropriation law of 1999 on FAOLEX and UNEP LEAP) and the ministry's successors for a page that defines an Expropriation Commission inside the Ministry of Public Works and Transport. The pages that opened covered the 1993 restitution law and a separate state restitution committee attached to the Council of Ministers, not this commission, so nothing can be said about it.

Agence d’Exécution des Travaux Urbains (.desc: A Beninese agency that acts as delegated project owner for public works: it awards and manages the study and construction contracts, supervises the works and handles the project money. It was created in October 1990 with capital of 100 million CFA francs and became a public limited company with a board in 2002; its shareholders are its own staff, local authorities, the Benin employers' federation and the Beninese state, and its capital reached 1.2 billion CFA francs in 2019.

sources.title: Projet de ratification de l'accord de prêt BOAD (Abomey streets), naming AGETUR as maître d'ouvrage délégué
AGETUR - Agence d'Exécution des Travaux Urbains, organisation profile

Société d’Études Régionales d’Habitat et.desc: A Beninese consulting firm in Cotonou that carries out urban planning, housing and local development studies and advises the state and local councils, and can also act as delegated project owner or land and property developer. It was set up as a limited company (SERHAU-SA) in March 1993, taking over from a government urban planning service created in 1986; at the start its capital was 48 per cent public, held by the state, the posts and electricity utilities and local authorities, and 52 per cent private.

sources.title: SERHAU-SA organisation profile
Development of the Urban Development Strategy of the Cotonou Urban Area (CDS-COTONOU)

Ministère des Infrastructures, des Trans.desc: The government department in Burkina Faso that handled roads, transport and housing. In a June 2005 address to a road sector seminar in Ouagadougou it put the country's road network at 15,300 kilometres of national, regional and departmental roads, and set out its aims of better targeted public road investment and a sustained maintenance strategy under the second transport sector programme.

sources.title: Discours d'ouverture du Ministre des Infrastructures, des Transports et de l'Habitat, séminaire de Ouagadougou

Ministère de l'Équipement et des Transpo.desc: The Malian government department responsible for national policy on public works and transport. Under the decree of 5 November 2002 setting out ministers' duties, it covered the building and upkeep of roads, railways, airfields and river ports, the development of land, river and air transport, meteorology and road traffic rules. By the decree of 4 September 2012 those duties had been split between a Ministry of Equipment and Territorial Development and a Ministry of Transport and Road Infrastructure.

sources.title: Décret n°02-498/P-RM du 5 novembre 2002 fixant les attributions spécifiques des membres du Gouvernement, Journal Officiel
Décret n°2012-486/P-RM du 4 septembre 2012 fixant les attributions spécifiques des membres du Gouvernement, Journal Officiel

Dangriga Town Council.desc: The elected local authority for the town of Dangriga, Belize, one of the towns listed in the Town Councils Act. It is a body corporate made up of a mayor and six other elected members, and it looks after the town's streets, drains and bridges, markets, parks and cemeteries, arranges rubbish collection, runs the Town Fund and makes local by-laws.

sources.title: Town Councils Act, Chapter 87

K & G Construction.note: Searched for the firm by name, with Belize, with Dangriga and with the principal's name. No company register entry, company website or news page describing the firm itself could be opened; the only pages found were unrelated builders of similar name in other countries.

CB Construction.note: Searched for the firm by name with Belize, San Ignacio and Cayo District. No company register entry, company website or trade directory page describing this firm could be opened.

Anthony Thurton & Associates.desc: Anthony Thurton and Associates Ltd, a Belizean consulting engineering firm. It designs and supervises small public works: in March 2023 it was awarded a 22-month contract worth 165,094 Belize dollars to review designs, prepare detailed designs and estimates and inspect construction for a village water supply scheme in Toledo District.

sources.title: Contract Award Information: Consultancy Services - Mafredi Water Supply, BNTF 10

Gobierno Autónomo Municipal de El Alto.desc: The city government of El Alto, Bolivia, on the altiplano above La Paz, covering about 385 square kilometres and divided into 14 municipal districts, 10 urban and 4 rural. The national statistics institute put its population at about 1.11 million in 2022, making it Bolivia's second largest city. It is run by an elected mayor and an 11-member municipal council, and its duties include basic services such as water and sanitation and building and maintaining school buildings.

sources.title: Informe Local Voluntario El Alto 2022
sources.publisher: Gobierno Autónomo Municipal de El Alto with UN-Habitat

Gobierno Autónomo Municipal de La Paz.desc: The city government of La Paz, Bolivia, organised into nine macro-districts each with its own sub-mayor's office, from Cotahuma to Zongo. Its services include the property cadastre, building permits, property subdivision and road works. Its final budget for 2022 was about 2.47 billion bolivianos, of which about 1.95 billion was spent.

sources.title: Informe de Contenido, Rendición Pública de Cuentas Final 2022
sources.publisher: Gobierno Autónomo Municipal de La Paz

Companhia de Água e Esgoto do Ceará (CAG.desc: The water and sewerage utility of the Brazilian state of Ceará, founded on 20 July 1971 by state law 9,499. It is a mixed-capital company controlled by the Ceará state government. In 2015 it operated in 151 of the state's 184 municipalities, supplied water to about 5.4 million people and sewerage to about 2.2 million, took water and sewerage revenue of 919.5 million reais and had 1,337 direct employees.

sources.title: Relatório da Administração e Demonstrações Financeiras 2015
sources.publisher: Companhia de Água e Esgoto do Ceará (CAGECE)

Prefeitura Municipal de São Paulo.desc: The city government of São Paulo, Brazil, and the executive side of the municipality, working alongside an elected city council that passes the laws and checks its accounts. It delivers municipal services through specialist secretariats, among them health, education and transport, some of them run with non-profit partners. Its budget for 2024, approved by the city council in December 2023, was 111.8 billion reais.

sources.title: Entendendo a Estrutura da Prefeitura de São Paulo na Administração Pública
sources.publisher: Conselho Participativo Municipal, Prefeitura de São Paulo

sources.title: Orçamento de R$ 111,8 bilhões proposto pela Prefeitura é aprovado pela Câmara

Municipality of Santos Secretariat of Go.desc: A secretariat of the city hall of Santos, Brazil, that works across the administration rather than running a single public service. In the city's 2025 government plan its tasks include putting Brazil's public efficiency law into local rules, information technology governance inside the council, a municipal tax incentive scheme for innovation, and supporting other secretariats' projects.

sources.title: Caderno do Plano de Metas e Plano de Diretrizes (plano de governo)

Ningbo Municipality Development and Refo.desc: A body of the Ningbo city government in Zhejiang province, China. Among the approvals it administers is the confirmation letter that a foreign investment project needs to show it fits national industrial policy, handled through the commission's service centre and its examination and approval office.

sources.title: The confirmation letters of foreign investment projects in conformity with national industrial policies

Gansu Provincial Development and Reform.desc: The Gansu provincial body in north-west China that draws up and publishes the province's annual list of major provincial construction projects, which sets out the schemes due to start or be prepared that year.

sources.title: Gansu Provincial NDRC's List of Major Provincial Construction Projects for 2026

Turpan Prefecture Water Resources Bureau.note: Chinese government websites for Turpan and for Xinjiang water authorities refuse automated fetching (robots), and searches in Chinese and English produced no other page describing this bureau, its legal basis or its duties. Nothing can be stated about it.

Jiangxi Administration of Navigation Aff.note: Searched in English and Chinese for this provincial waterway body and tried the transport ministry's published documents, which did not render as text. Fenghua Investment Co., Ltd..note: Searched in Chinese and English for a company register entry, bond prospectus or company page for this Fenghua (Ningbo) entity. Nothing naming this exact company could be opened, and the local government sites that might carry it refuse automated fetching.

Projet de Facilitation du Commerce et du.note: This is the implementation unit set up inside the Ivorian government to run one donor-financed corridor project. Searches found only project documents about the corridor programme itself, none describing the unit as a standing organisation with its own legal basis, staff or size, so nothing can be said about it beyond its role in that project.

Mission d’Appui à la Conduite d’Opératio.desc: A support unit for Cote d'Ivoire's municipal development programme PACOM, housed inside the BNETD, the country's national office for technical studies and development (formerly DCGTx). It acted as secretary to the inter-ministerial committee that headed the programme, handled its day-to-day business and central records, and helped town councils supervise consultants, design project work, and prepare environmental impact studies and resettlement plans.

sources.title: Upgrading of Low Income Settlements: Country Assessment Report, Cote d'Ivoire
sources.publisher: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Urban Upgrading programme

Project Coordination Unit, Ministry of H.note: Searched for a page describing this coordination unit inside Cameroon's housing and urban development ministry as a body in its own right. Only project documents referring to its work on one donor-financed programme were found, with nothing on its legal basis, staffing or budget, so nothing can be said about it.

Unité de Coordination de Projets (UCoP),.note: Searched in French and English for a decree, ministry page or news report describing a standing Unite de Coordination de Projets in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The pages that opened concerned other Congolese infrastructure bodies and newer units, none of them this one, so it cannot be described.

Bureau Central de Coordination (BCECO),.desc: A Congolese public service created by presidential decree 039/2001 of 8 August 2001 and supervised by the Ministry of Finance. It manages, coordinates and carries out development projects paid for from the state's own money and by foreign donors, covering the whole life of a project from preparation to closure, in fields including education, health, local development and roads. Its portal lists 164 projects across the country's 26 provinces.

sources.title: À propos
sources.publisher: Bureau Central de Coordination (BCECO), Democratic Republic of the Congo

Secrétariat Permanent, Projet de Dévelop.desc: The permanent secretariat of the Urban Development Project in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, placed under the national Ministry of Urban Planning and Housing. For the Kinshasa urban development and resilience project it coordinated preparation on behalf of the city-province of Kinshasa, with an environmental and a social safeguards specialist on its staff, screening and classifying sub-projects and circulating the reports, before handing those tasks to a separate coordination unit once construction began.

sources.title: Cadre de Gestion Environnementale et Sociale, Projet de Développement Urbain et de Résilience de Kinshasa (PDUR-K)
sources.publisher: Secrétariat Permanent du Projet de Développement Urbain, Ministère de l'Urbanisme et Habitat, DR Congo
